findings.claim: Ruling (b) fixes only the `<slug>.txt` collision. On a second DEFECTIVE verdict, `fail` still moves the slug's approved files, and under D-38 its round, review, ruling and cite files too, into a `gauntlet/failed/<slug>.approved/` that already holds run 1's files under the same slug-derived names. So the collision that finding 2.02 names ('`<slug>.txt` and `<slug>.approved/` exist') is still there.
findings.failure_scenario: Run 1 on slug S is judged defective. `fail` creates `failed/S.approved/` holding `S.txt`, `S-summary.md`, the hash and (per D-38) `S.review.1.txt` and the other round files. Run 2 on S is judged defective too. `fail` moves `failed/S.txt` to `S.approved/verdict.1.txt`, copies the new verdict, then moves run 2's same-named files into `S.approved/`. A no-clobber move exits non-zero, so the run fails instead of cancelling at `kill`. Archon resume then re-runs `fail`, which moves run 2's own verdict to `verdict.2.txt` and copies it again. A clobbering move instead silently replaces run 1's plan and round record, so `verdict.1.txt` sits next to files it did not judge.

findings.claim: D-39 keeps the latest verdict at the fixed name `gauntlet/failed/<slug>.txt` for good. D-38's first-script-node trigger fires 'when a failed record exists', so after one defect it is true for every later hearing of that slug, not only the first rerun.
findings.failure_scenario: Slug S is judged defective once. A new run on S gets through plan-review round 2, then dies on a failed node. The owner starts a fresh gauntlet-run on S, because the file route reruns the same slug. Plan review's first script node finds `failed/S.txt` and sets aside run 2's own round 1-2 files. Paid rounds are lost and restart at round 1, and the move collides with the files already in `S.approved/`. This happens on every fresh run on S, forever.

findings.claim: Ruling (b) makes `fail` move and rewrite `<slug>.txt` and write `verdict.<n>.txt`. That contradicts the Homes row ('written once by `fail`') and contracts.md row H24 (`cp -n`). The ruling does not amend either row.
findings.failure_scenario: Phase 2 builds `fail` from the ruling, and a fence or contract check built from row :401 or H24 then flags the second write of `failed/<slug>.txt`, or the new `verdict.<n>.txt` name, as a breach. Or the builder follows the row and keeps `cp -n`, which leaves the defect in place.
